questions.prompt: What is special about the Main component's dependencies?

options.text: Main depends on everything, but nothing depends on Main
Main depends on nothing and nothing depends on it

questions.explanation: Main is the outermost, dirtiest module: it depends on everything and is depended on by nothing, so its concrete knowledge is quarantined.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the composition root and Main are TRUE? Select all that apply.

options.text: It is the place where the `new` keyword for volatile concretions belongs
Nothing else in the system depends on Main
Inner layers should construct their own volatile dependencies with `new`
Constructor injection is the preferred way to supply dependencies

questions.explanation: The composition root constructs concretions and Main is depended on by nothing; constructor injection is preferred. Inner layers should receive collaborators by injection, not construct volatile ones themselves.

questions.prompt: The single place that constructs concrete implementations and injects them into abstractions is called the ______ root.
questions.explanation: The composition root, usually near the program's entry point, wires the object graph.

questions.prompt: Does using a DI container guarantee you are following the Dependency Inversion Principle?

options.text: Yes — that's what containers are for
No — if inner code still imports concretions, DIP is violated regardless of how objects are built
Yes — as long as the container is popular

questions.explanation: A container only constructs objects. DIP is about what you depend on in source; importing concretions violates it even with a container.

questions.prompt: Match each injection style or tool to its description.

pairs.right: Dependencies set after construction (risks half-built objects)
A library that builds the object graph from registered mappings
The one place concretions are wired to abstractions

questions.explanation: Prefer constructor injection; a container is optional tooling; the composition root centralizes wiring.

questions.prompt: Order the construction steps in a composition root.

items.text: Construct use cases, injecting the interfaces
Construct driving adapters (controllers) with the use cases

questions.explanation: You build outward-to-inward-to-outward: config, then concrete driven adapters, inject them into use cases, then wire controllers to those use cases.
